DAY 1 · FRIDAY, OCT 2

Kochi → Munnar

Spice garden, then an easy evening in Munnar
Longest single item today is the drive itself — 130 km, about 4 hours. Everyone will be running on little sleep, so the afternoon activities are kept short and close to town.
Early AM

Land in Kochi

Direct flight from home. Allow 20–30 minutes for immigration and baggage before meeting the driver.

5:20 AM – 9:00 AM

Transit: Kochi → Munnar

~117 km, ~3.5 hours. Stop for breakfast or coffee at Cheeyappara or Valara Falls en route — a natural stretch break on the hill climb.

~9:00 – 10:00 AM

Cinnamon Gardens Spice Plantation

13 km before Munnar town, right on NH85 — no detour needed. A relaxed guided walk through cardamom, pepper, vanilla, and cinnamon, ~45–60 minutes.

~10:15 AM

Arrive Munnar, check in & rest

Standard check-in is 12 PM — request early check-in given the 10:15 AM arrival, and get it confirmed in writing beforehand.

Evening (pick one)

Rose Garden — or — Pothamedu Sunset Point

Two light, low-effort options, not both: Rose Garden is a small stepped floriculture nursery close to town, an easy stroll if energy allows. Pothamedu Sunset Point is a genuine valley viewpoint over tea, coffee, and cardamom plantations — a better pick if everyone's up for a short walk and a proper view at golden hour. Decide on the day based on how everyone's holding up.

Evening

Back to hotel · easy dinner

A proper wind-down before an early start for Eravikulam tomorrow.

Nearby: DTPC Boat Jetty & River Walkwayoptional

~5–10 min walk from the hotel. Pedal boating on a small lake (₹150–200/person) plus an adjoining riverside walkway and children's park. Worth knowing before you go: reviews are mixed — fun but crowded on weekends, with some complaints about water cleanliness, thin life jackets, and the park's upkeep. A casual filler if there's a spare hour, not worth building the day around.

2

DAY 2 · SATURDAY, OCT 3

Munnar

Eravikulam wildlife, waterfalls & Kundala Lake boating
7:15 – 7:45 AM

Drive to Eravikulam (5th Mile entry)

North through town, ahead of holiday traffic building up.

8:00 – 10:30 AM

Eravikulam National Park (Rajamalai)

Forest Dept mini-bus to the entry point, then either the senior electric buggy or a gentle 300–400 m stroll along the paved crest road — Nilgiri Tahr grazing against the backdrop of Anamudi peak. Tickets must be booked in advance (see the box above) — daily entry is capped and Saturdays draw more demand.

10:45 – 11:00 AM

Nyamakad Waterfall

Quick roadside photo stop by the bridge on the way back down — zero trekking involved.

11:30 AM – 1:00 PM

Lunch in Munnar town

Saravana Bhavan or Rapsy Restaurant (Main Bazaar, known for parathas and biryani) — or a garden café on Mattupetty Road.

1:15 – 2:00 PM

Drive to Kundala Lake

Scenic road east, passing but not stopping at the crowded Mattupetty and Echo Point stalls.

2:15 – 3:30 PM

Kundala Lake

A short, flat stroll through lakeside pine and eucalyptus, then a shaded Kashmiri shikara boat ride for the family — or a solo kayak if you'd rather paddle yourself. Consistently rated the most scenic and least crowded of Munnar's three boating spots.

3:45 – 5:00 PM

Drive back to the resort

Timed to beat the late-afternoon mist thickening on the hill roads.

5:30 PM onward

Relaxed evening

Hotel balcony, hot tea, dinner, and packing ahead of the Oct 4 transit to Thekkady.

3

DAY 3 · SUNDAY, OCT 4

Munnar → Thekkady

Chinnakanal, Anayirankal & an evening martial arts show
Boating tickets for Oct 4 sold out, so the afternoon is now a relaxed, low-key Thekkady stretch instead of a wildlife-focused one — spice plantation, spa, and the town itself, still anchored by the fixed 6 PM Kalaripayattu slot.
7:30 – 8:00 AM

Depart Munnar via Gap Road

Through Devikulam, climbing onto the Gap Road corridor — tea and cardamom country opening into wider valley views.

~8:15 – 8:30 AM

Chinnakanal Waterfall (Power House Falls)

~15 km from Munnar, right on the road. Quick roadside stop, no trekking — 10–15 minutes.

~8:40 – 9:10 AM

Anayirankal Dam

~22 km from Munnar, also directly on the route. Scenic earthen dam and reservoir — a photo stop (~15–20 min), or add a short shikara/pedal boat ride if there's appetite for it (adds ~20–30 min).

~9:15 AM – 12:00 PM

Continue via Pooppara to Kumily/Thekkady

Remaining ~70–95 km of the same road, descending through spice-growing terrain toward Kumily.

~12:00 – 12:30 PM

Arrive Thekkady, check in

Still a genuinely relaxed arrival despite the two stops — no rush anywhere.

12:30 – 1:30 PM

Lunch

Wander Kumily, rest at the hotel, or take it slow — the whole afternoon is unhurried now.

1:30 – 2:30 PM

Spice plantation guided walk

Widely available in Thekkady/Kumily — cardamom, pepper, vanilla, cinnamon. ~45–90 minutes, low effort, genuinely worthwhile.

2:30 – 3:30 PM

Ayurvedic massage / spa

A relaxed option, especially welcome for your parents after several days of travel.

3:30 – 4:30 PM

Kumily town walk

Spice markets, chocolate shops, local handicrafts — easy on foot.

4:30 – 5:30 PM

Rest & freshen up

Back at the hotel before the evening show.

6:00 – 7:00 PM

Kalaripayattu show

Kadathanadan Kalari Centre in Kumily — a well-regarded venue for this martial art, right in Thekkady. Doing the show here also frees up Oct 6 in Kochi, which is otherwise your tightest day.

Evening

Dinner & rest

An easy close to the day.

DAY 4 · MONDAY, OCT 5

Thekkady → Alleppey

Into the backwaters — sleeping on land tonight
~140 km, ~4 hours via Kottayam. Depart by 8:30–9:00 AM so you clear Kottayam town by late morning, ahead of its midday congestion — a natural lunch stop at Kumarakom (right on the way) adds a further buffer before the final stretch into Alleppey.
8:00 – 8:30 AM

Breakfast & check-out

Keys Prima, Thekkady.

8:30 – 9:00 AM

Depart Thekkady

~140 km total to Alleppey via Kottayam.

~11:00 – 11:30 AM

Reach Kottayam / Kumarakom area

~85–90 km, ~2–2.5 hours. Passing through late morning, well ahead of the midday bottleneck through Kottayam town.

~12:00 – 1:00 PM

Lunch at Kumarakom

Right on the route — a backwater-view lunch stop rather than a detour. Breaks up the drive and adds extra buffer before Alleppey.

~1:45 – 2:15 PM

Arrive Alleppey, check in

~30–35 km remaining, ~45 min–1 hour. Land resort stay, not a houseboat — proper beds and a settled night after a run of travel days.

Afternoon

Rest & free time

Genuinely open — also a good window to confirm tomorrow's day cruise timing and details directly with the resort.

5:30 – 6:30 PM

Sunset shikara ride

Kerala sunset falls around 6:10–6:15 PM in early October — timed to catch it. Short canoe ride through the narrow backwater canals, a gentle first taste of Alleppey before tomorrow's full cruise.

Evening

Dinner

At the resort — no need to go anywhere after the shikara ride.

Night

Peaceful night on land

No rocking, no mosquito nets to manage — a genuinely restful night before an active last full day.

DAY 5 · TUESDAY, OCT 6

Alleppey → Kochi

Backwaters, Folklore Museum, Kathakali & a late flight home
Confirm with the resort beforehand: since Muhamma sits ~11 km from the Punnamada cruise hub, check whether the 9:30 AM cruise start below needs an earlier pickup time to account for that distance. From there, the day builds around two fixed points — Kerala Folklore Museum closes at 5:30 PM (it sits in Thevara, roughly on the way from Alleppey before you cross into Fort Kochi, so no detour needed), and Kathakali runs a fixed 6:00–7:00 PM slot, so the evening is built around that anchor rather than a lingering sunset walk.
9:30 AM – 12:30 PM

Backwater day cruise

The shorter public slot, chosen deliberately to keep the rest of the day light.

12:30 – 1:30 PM

Lunch

Onboard or riverside, before checkout and the drive to Kochi.

1:30 PM

Depart Alleppey

Confirm late checkout or luggage storage with the resort beforehand — checkout is 11 AM, well before this.

~3:00 – 3:15 PM

Arrive Kerala Folklore Museum (Thevara)

~1.5 hours from Alleppey, roughly on the route into Kochi. A private family collection of 5,000+ artifacts across three floors, each representing a different Kerala architectural style — consistently well-reviewed, unlike some of the more touristy stops in the area.

3:15 – 4:30 PM

Folklore Museum visit

₹100 entry, ₹100/group for photography. Closes 5:30 PM, so this window keeps a comfortable margin.

4:30 – 5:00 PM

Drive to Fort Kochi

~9–12 km, ~20–30 minutes.

5:00 – 5:50 PM

Chinese Fishing Nets waterfront walk

Skipping the Kathakali makeup-viewing session to keep this a real window, not a rushed walk-by — early golden hour rather than the full sunset, but a genuine look at the water and the nets in action.

6:00 – 7:00 PM

Kathakali performance

Kerala Kathakali Centre, next to Santa Cruz Basilica — a different art form from the Kalaripayattu you already saw in Thekkady. Book ahead given October demand.

7:15 – 8:30 PM

Dinner

A proper last meal, not an eat-and-go.

8:30 – 10:30 PM

Buffer & rest

No booked room — luggage stays in the cab (driver's with you the whole trip, so low risk; keep passports/valuables on hand rather than in the trunk). A relaxed café or restaurant terrace works fine for winding down. If someone genuinely needs to lie down or shower, book an hourly room on the spot via OYO or StayUncle — solid same-day availability in Fort Kochi.

10:30 – 11:00 PM

Transit: Fort Kochi → Cochin Airport

~40–45 km, ~1–1.25 hours by distance alone. This timing gives a comfortable buffer before airport check-in closes. Leaving earlier, around 9–10 PM, trades a little of the buffer above for extra airport downtime — a reasonable call if the family prefers zero time pressure.

Where to eat in Fort Kochi

Dinner, Oct 6
Fort House Restaurantrecommended

Highest-rated of the group, right by the sea with a heritage setting — with the evening now unhurried, this is worth the slightly longer, more memorable meal.

Fort Paragon Restaurantreliable

Excellent Kerala classics and biryani, AC indoor seating — a proper sit-down meal, easy either way.

Maple Sea Food Restaurantsfastest

Casual, beachside, and quick — fresh seafood at a good price if you'd still rather keep it simple.

Seagull and Fusion Bay are both well-loved for seafood but known for longer waits — now genuinely worth considering too, given the evening has more slack.

DAY 6 · WEDNESDAY, OCT 7

Fly home

Early AM

Fly Kochi → Home

Direct flight, landing back home before sunrise.

Know before you go

Book the Kalaripayattu and Kathakali tickets in advance

Both can sell out, especially in October when tourist traffic picks up. Don't plan on walking in.

Periyar boat safari for Oct 4 is sold out

Boating tickets for that date were gone by the time we checked. The Oct 4 afternoon now runs on a spice plantation walk, an Ayurvedic spa session, and a Kumily town walk instead — still anchored by the fixed 6 PM Kalaripayattu slot. Worth calling the reserve office directly (+91-4869-222027) if you want to double-check availability closer to the date, in case of cancellations.

Book the private car for the whole trip — still not done

Standard practice in Kerala rather than a luxury — point-to-point taxis aren't reliable once you're outside the cities. Every day's timing in this itinerary assumes one car and driver for all six days, so this is worth locking in early rather than left for the last minute.

Leave Munnar and Thekkady with a little extra time

Hill roads are naturally slower than the map suggests. None of the drives on this trip are traffic-prone, but they do run long.

Kochi's evening rush hour is real

5:00–7:30 PM in the city (especially around Vyttila Junction) can turn a 10-minute hop into 25–30 minutes. This is exactly the window on Oct 6 evening — budget accordingly.

No booked room for Oct 6 evening — luggage stays in the cab

With a private car and driver the whole trip, this is low-risk — just keep passports and valuables with you rather than in the trunk. If genuine rest is needed, book an hourly room ad-hoc via OYO or StayUncle; both have solid same-day coverage in Fort Kochi.
